chunks: From him, from Ibn Mahbub, from Abu Jarir al-Rawwasi, who said:
I heard Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) while he was saying: 'O God, I ask You for ease/comfort at the time of death and forgiveness at the time of reckoning.' He would repeat it.

key_terms.الرَّاحَةَ: Ease, comfort, or relief (specifically in the context of death)
key_terms.الْعَفْوَ: Pardon, forgiveness, or exemption from punishment
key_terms.عِنْدَ الْحِسَابِ: At the time of reckoning/accounting (on the Day of Judgment)
key_terms.يُرَدِّدُهَا: He would repeat it (indicating a frequent or habitual practice)

ai.seo_question: What is the specific supplication for death and reckoning taught by the Imams?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this supplication highlights the Imam’s emphasis on preparing for the two pivotal transitions of death and the Day of Judgment. By repeatedly seeking 'ease' (al-raha) and 'pardon' (al-'afw), it underscores the Shia scholarly view that divine mercy is the ultimate safeguard against the rigors of the final accounting.
